title: Bruges lace tile
subtitle: A small square assembled from interlaced crochet ribbon strips in the Bruges lace tradition
excerpt: Bruges crochet works narrow ribbon strips — three stitches wide — in long lengths, then bends, folds, and joins them to form geometric tiles. This small square assembles four ribbon strips into a 10 cm tile with an interlaced centre where the strips cross. The construction looks complex but each strip is entirely straightforward to crochet.
sourceNotes: Bruges lacework originates in Belgium and was adapted into crochet in the late 19th century. Documented in Weldon's Practical Needlework, Volume 6 (1891), Bruges crochet chapter.
heroPrompt: A Bruges lace crochet tile in fine cream cotton thread on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Four interlaced ribbon strips forming a geometric square, 10 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished Bruges lace tile measures 10 × 10 cm in 4-ply cotton thread with a 2.5 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Bruges lace tile
chartDefinition.caption: Each ribbon strip is a continuous 3-stitch-wide htr strip. Four strips interlock at the centre. Assembly joins strips at crossing points and corners with sl st.

stitches.label: sl st join at crossing point

glossaryTerms.definition: A narrow crochet strip, usually 3–5 stitches wide, worked in continuous rows with a turning chain. Used as the structural element in Bruges lace, bent and joined to form geometric patterns.

content.text: as the structural components, then bends and joins them to form geometric shapes. The tile here assembles four ribbon strips in a simple interlace pattern: two horizontal and two vertical, with each pair passing over and under the other at the four crossing points in the centre.

The four strips are identical. Work them all to the same length first, then join. The interlace requires physically weaving one strip over the other before joining with slip stitches at the crossing points — this is the one step that requires three-dimensional thinking.

attrs.title: Materials for one tile
attrs.body: About 12 g of 4-ply cotton thread. A 2.5 mm hook. Blocking mat and pins essential.

content.text: Ch 5. Htr in 3rd ch from hook, htr in each ch to end. (3 htr.) *Ch 3, turn. Htr in 2nd ch, htr in 3rd ch, sl st into next htr (joins turning ch to strip edge). Htr across.* Rep from * until strip is 12 cm long. Fasten off.

Lay two strips horizontally and two vertically. Weave the vertical strips over and under the horizontal strips at the four crossing points. Pin to blocking mat to hold in position. Sl st at each crossing point and at each corner where strips meet. Block flat with all edges pinned straight.
Work the tunisian crochet square for a different advanced technique — tunisian produces a flat mesh without the strip-assembly complexity of Bruges lace.
